openvpn.dnsHint: Overrides this host's DNS for OpenVPN clients. Leave empty to use the core's default DNS.
openvpn.priorityHint: Lower numbers are tried first when the client fails over between OpenVPN hosts in the downloaded file.

mtproto.noExtraSettings: MTProto hosts need no additional settings here — the fake-TLS domain and secrets are configured on the core instance and per user.

l2tp.noExtraSettings: L2TP/IPsec hosts need no additional settings here — the pre-shared key and IPsec parameters are configured on the core instance, and credentials are per user.

hostsDialog.mihomoEchConfig.info: Optional base64 ECH config for Mihomo. Leave empty to retrieve the current config from DNS.
hostsDialog.mihomoEchQueryServerName.info: Optional domain used by Mihomo for ECH DNS queries. This also enables ECH when the static config is empty.
hostsDialog.singBoxEchConfig.info: Optional base64 or PEM ECH config for Sing-box. Base64 input is converted to the required PEM line array; leave empty to query DNS.
hostsDialog.singBoxEchQueryServerName.info: Optional domain used by Sing-box for ECH HTTPS-record queries. This also enables ECH when the static config is empty. Requires Sing-box 1.13.0 or later.

nodeModal.additionalCoresHint: Run more cores alongside the primary one on this node. Xray cores cannot be added here.
nodeModal.noAdditionalCores: No other core can run alongside the selected primary core.

sectionDesc.l2tpSettings: The L2TP/IPsec server, its client address pool and its IPsec settings.
sectionDesc.mtInstances: Each instance is an independent MTProto listener shared by every authorized user.
sectionDesc.sbInbounds: Hysteria2 inbound listeners for this sing-box core
sectionDesc.ovInstances: Each instance is an independent openvpn process on a distinct protocol/port.
sectionDesc.ovPki: Server certificate authority, certificate, and key management.

singbox.inboundsHint: Each inbound is a separate Hysteria2 listener on this sing-box core.
singbox.emptyInbounds: No inbounds yet. Click "Add inbound" to create a Hysteria2 listener.

fields.ignoreClientBandwidthHint: Ignore the bandwidth values reported by the client and always use the values above.

obfs.title: Obfuscation
obfs.enableHint: Wraps the QUIC handshake in the Salamander obfuscator. Every client must use the same password.

tls.title: TLS
tls.alwaysEnabledHint: Hysteria2 always requires TLS; it cannot be disabled for this inbound.
tls.requiredHint: This protocol always requires TLS; it cannot be disabled for this inbound.
tls.acmeOwnsCert: ACME is enabled below and manages the certificate automatically. The manual certificate fields are disabled.

ss.title: Shadowsocks
ss.serverKeyHint: Base64 server key for the 2022 cipher. Per-user passwords are injected automatically.
ss.legacyHint: Legacy single-user password. Prefer a 2022-blake3 method for multi-user.

l2tp.blurb: One L2TP/IPsec server. Clients authenticate the IPsec layer with the shared key (PSK) and the PPP layer with their own username and password. The listener is always UDP 1701, with IKE on 500 and NAT-T on 4500.

fields.inboundTagHint: Identifies this server across the panel and names its files on the node.
fields.serverAddrHint: The public IP or hostname clients connect to.
fields.pskHint: Every client needs this key; it is shown on their subscription page.
fields.pskEmptyHint: Leave empty and the panel generates a random key when you save. On an existing core a new key replaces the old one, so every client has to be updated.
fields.poolHint: Private IPv4 range handed to clients, between /8 and /29.
fields.localIpHint: Must sit inside the pool. Empty means the pool's first address.
fields.egressInterfaceHint: Optional. Send this pool's traffic out a specific interface on the node.
fields.dnsHint: One IPv4 address per line. Empty means 1.1.1.1 and 8.8.8.8.
fields.ikeProposalsHint: One per line. Empty means the node's defaults.
fields.espProposalsHint: One per line. Empty means the node's defaults.
fields.legacyClientsHint: Adds older 3DES/modp1024 algorithms for very old devices. Weaker; leave off unless you need it.

fields.fakeTlsDomainHint: Any real, publicly reachable domain works - it does not need to be owned by you or have any TLS certificate of its own. Every connecting client is validated against the secret alone; this domain is only used to disguise unauthenticated probes as ordinary HTTPS traffic to that site.
fields.adTagHint: Optional. Register this proxy with Telegram's @MTProxybot (server address, port, and a client secret) to get a tag, then paste it here to show a sponsor channel to connecting clients. Leave empty for a plain, un-promoted proxy. Setting this routes traffic for this instance through Telegram's middle-proxy servers instead of connecting to Telegram directly, which adds one extra network hop.

mtproto.instancesHint: Each instance is an independent fake-TLS listener (port + disguise domain), shared by every authorized user.
mtproto.keepAtLeastOne: At least one instance is required.
mtproto.emptyInstances: No instances yet. Click "Add instance" to create one.

bulk.l2tpActivateDesc: Generate L2TP/IPsec passwords for existing users who have L2TP access but never received one
bulk.l2tpActivateDescription: Generates an L2TP/IPsec password for existing users who have L2TP access through their group but never received one.
bulk.l2tpActivateSafety: Users who already have a password are never touched or regenerated, even if selected below.
bulk.mtprotoActivateDesc: Generate missing MTProto secrets for existing users
bulk.mtprotoActivateDescription: Generates an MTProto proxy secret for existing users who have MTProto access through their group but never received one - e.g. users created before MTProto was enabled on their group.
bulk.mtprotoActivateSafety: Users who already have a secret are never touched or regenerated, even if selected below.

statistics.noConnectedNodes: No connected nodes to report on.
statistics.inboundUsageDescription: Total traffic per inbound over time
statistics.inboundDataHint: Inbound history builds up from the moment it is enabled.
settings.connectionLimit.title: Connection limit
settings.connectionLimit.loadError: Failed to load connection limit settings
settings.connectionLimit.saveFailed: Failed to save connection limit settings
settings.connectionLimit.detection.title: Device detection
settings.connectionLimit.detection.descr: Counts how many devices are using each subscription at once, from the addresses the nodes report and the hardware IDs clients send.
settings.connectionLimit.enabled.title: Enable detection
settings.connectionLimit.enabled.descrip: Check online users on a schedule and record how many devices each has.
settings.connectionLimit.monitorOnly.des: Record what is seen without restricting anyone. Leave on until the numbers look right.
settings.connectionLimit.limits.title: Device allowance
settings.connectionLimit.deviceLimit.des: Above this many devices counts as over the limit.
settings.connectionLimit.warnAt.title: Warn at
settings.connectionLimit.warnAt.descript: Highlight from this many devices, before the limit is passed.
settings.connectionLimit.interval.title: Check every (seconds)
settings.connectionLimit.concurrency.des: Addresses seen further apart than this are treated as the same person after an address change.
settings.connectionLimit.accuracy.title: Avoiding false positives
settings.connectionLimit.accuracy.descri: A CDN shows one device as many addresses, and a tunnel shows many devices as one. These settings keep either from being mistaken for a device count.
settings.connectionLimit.infra.title: Treat as shared infrastructure at
settings.connectionLimit.infra.descripti: An address seen under this many different users is a tunnel or NAT, not a device, and is ignored.
settings.connectionLimit.cdn.title: CDN address ranges
settings.connectionLimit.cdn.description: One range per line. All of a user's addresses inside these ranges count as one device, since a CDN hides how many are behind it. The built-in list covers Cloudflare and Fastly.
settings.connectionLimit.validation.warn: Warn value cannot be above the device limit
connectionLimit.badge.title: {{count}} device(s)
settings.connectionLimit.review.title: Devices per subscription
settings.connectionLimit.review.descript: What the last check saw. Nothing here has been acted on.
settings.connectionLimit.review.empty: Nothing recorded for this filter yet.
settings.connectionLimit.review.disabled: Detection is off. Turn it on in the settings above to start collecting.
settings.connectionLimit.scope.title: Who is checked
settings.connectionLimit.scope.descripti: Leave both empty to check every user. Choosing any narrows checking to those users only.
settings.connectionLimit.isp.title: Look up the provider behind an address
settings.connectionLimit.isp.description: Shows the ISP name when reviewing a user. Only when a case is opened, never during checking — but it does send that address to a third-party service.
settings.connectionLimit.override.title: Device allowance
settings.connectionLimit.override.descri: Leave empty to use the default of {{limit}}.
settings.connectionLimit.override.exempt: They are skipped entirely and no count is recorded.
settings.connectionLimit.override.notePl: Why, for the next person looking
settings.connectionLimit.override.invali: Enter a number of 1 or more, or leave it empty
connectionLimit.reason.cdn: {{count}} CDN address(es), counted as one device
connectionLimit.reason.infrastructure: {{count}} shared or tunnel address(es), not counted
connectionLimit.reason.earlier: {{count}} further network(s) seen earlier, not at the same time
connectionLimit.reason.concurrent: {{count}} of them live at the same moment
connectionLimit.reason.cdn_without_hwid: behind a CDN with no hardware id reported — several devices would look like one
connectionLimit.reason.nodes: carried traffic on {{count}} nodes, across {{cycles}} checks in a row
settings.connectionLimit.persistence.tit: Checks a pattern must hold for
settings.connectionLimit.persistence.des: Several nodes are only reported after holding for this many checks in a row.
connectionLimit.reason.fetched_not_count: {{count}} device(s) fetched the subscription but were not counted — holding the configuration is not being connected
settings.connectionLimit.fetched.title: Count devices that only fetched the subscription
settings.connectionLimit.fetched.descrip: Fetching the subscription is not being connected. Behind a CDN they count regardless.
settings.connectionLimit.nodeTraffic.des: Below this a node is treated as merely tried, not used. Zero counts every node.
settings.connectionLimit.enforcement.des: Warning, then 10, 30 and 60 minutes, then until lifted. Counted over three days.
settings.connectionLimit.enforcement.tog: Act on users over the limit
Off by default. Nothing is done to anyone until this is on.
settings.connectionLimit.violations.on: Counted over the last {{hours}} hours. A user who behaves for that long starts again at the first step.
settings.connectionLimit.violations.off: Acting on users is off, so nothing new will be added here.
connectionLimit.reason.carrier_pool: {{count}} addresses came from carrier pools ({{items}}) — a mobile network hands one phone a different address per connection, so each pool counts once
settings.connection-limit.title: Connection limit
settings.connection-limit-review.title: Devices per subscription
connectionLimit.reason.nodes_at_once: on {{count}} nodes at the same moment: {{items}}
settings.hwid.scope.title: Groups the policy covers
settings.hwid.scope.description: Empty covers everyone. With groups chosen, users outside them are not covered at all.
settings.hwid.scope.label: Groups
connectionLimit.reason.hwid_by_model: counted as {{count}} device(s) by phone model: {{items}}
connectionLimit.reason.nodes_at_once_pen: seen on {{count}} nodes at once ({{cycles}} check(s) so far) — not counted yet; a brief overlap is usually a node switch: {{items}}
settings.connectionLimit.deviceWindow.de: How far back to look for the apps and devices that fetched the subscription. Longer than the node window, because an app keeps a configuration and runs a while without fetching again — a short window loses a device that is still in use.
settings.connectionLimit.addresses.title: Addresses and providers
settings.connectionLimit.addresses.descr: The networks this user was last seen on, and the provider behind each.
settings.connectionLimit.addresses.looku: Provider lookup is off, so only the addresses are shown. Turn it on in the settings above.
settings.connectionLimit.addresses.empty: No addresses recorded for this user.
contentFilter.title: Content filtering
settings.content-filter.title: Content filtering
contentFilter.subtitle: Build a profile from ready-made categories and apply it to one endpoint, so the config you hand out is restricted while nobody else is affected.
contentFilter.name: Profile name
contentFilter.emptyBody: A profile is a set of categories to block. Create one, tick what should be unreachable, then choose which endpoint it applies to.
contentFilter.wholeGroupNote: The whole group is blocked, so every service in it is already covered.
contentFilter.strictBody: Some connections hide their destination name, so no category can match them. With this on they are refused — which also blocks the occasional legitimate app that connects by address. With it off, they pass, and that is a way around the filter.
contentFilter.allowHint: Reachable even when a category above covers it.
contentFilter.blockHint: Blocked even when no category covers it.
contentFilter.saved: Saved and pushed to every endpoint it covers
contentFilter.confirmDelete: Remove this profile and lift it everywhere it applies?
contentFilter.whereBody: Only customers whose config uses one of these endpoints are affected.
contentFilter.addEndpointBody: Endpoints that cannot enforce destination rules are listed with the reason and cannot be chosen.
contentFilter.noEndpoints: Not applied anywhere yet, so nobody is affected by this profile.
contentFilter.applied: Applied and confirmed on the node
contentFilter.checkBody: Ask the node what it would do with one address, without connecting anything.
contentFilter.scope.endpoint: One endpoint, on every node that has it
contentFilter.noFleetEndpoints: No filterable endpoint exists on any node yet.
contentFilter.everyNodeWith: {{endpoint}} — on every node that has it
contentFilter.section.categoriesHint: Switch a whole group off, or open one and pick the services inside it.
contentFilter.section.hardeningHint: Two settings that decide what happens beyond the categories above.
contentFilter.section.listsHint: Curated blocklists that ship with the node — picking one costs the rule nothing extra.
contentFilter.wildcardHint: example.com and *.example.com both cover every subdomain. =example.com covers only that exact name.
contentFilter.noProbeNode: No connected node currently carries this endpoint, so there is nothing to ask.
